name: Hutchinson Rock
generated_description:
Hutchinson Rock is a 4,423-foot summit in Virginia. The Hutchinson Rock Trail covers 0.5 miles with about 62 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 37.14239, -81.41706 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 80 miles west of Roanoke, Virginia. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Late May through October is the main season. Snow and ice linger into spring and return early in fall at this latitude and elevation; in winter this becomes a different, more serious undertaking requiring traction devices and warm layers.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go.
